A divergent replica remains eligible without repair.
Healthy copies are demoted on false or correlated failure observations.
A master is demoted before a usable successor exists.
A lone unhealthy master loses its assignment without a successor.
A live node remains Down indefinitely.
An empty or stale node is crowned master.
Multiple processes serve as master for a partition.
A masterless partition is never refilled.
A replica is activated or promoted before completing synchronization.
Deletion destroys the last usable copy.
Deletion interrupts reconstruction or repeats on a terminating pod.
Force deletion bypasses evidence and drain conditions.
Topology application is lost or never retried.
Delayed topology arrives after a newer authority or assignment.
A deposed leader still issues topology commands.
Repeated resync failure never removes an unsafe replica from serving.
Endpoint membership advertises an unserving node.
Fetch is not resumed after a transient disconnection.
The applied position advances past a range that was not applied (e.g. a forwarded write taken as WAL progress).
A newer value arrives by forwarding and an older WAL change is then applied over it.
A delete is applied and an older put then resurrects the key.
The process crashes after applying changes and before the position is saved, so the same range is re-applied or skipped inconsistently.
A batch from an old session or lineage is applied.
A replica whose required history is gone is treated as synchronised.
A lagging or unobservable replica is treated as safe for reads, promotion or deletion.
WAL is retained until the master's disk is exhausted.
Delete history is discarded while a change older than the delete can still be applied.
The apply decision is made against a position read before a stall, retry or lock wait, so a change admitted against an old cursor is written after the cursor moved.
After a rebuild, changes from the previous session, or metadata inherited from the source, are applied.
A key is changed by a path that does not capture an order label (bulk operation, internal delete), so the change cannot be ordered against the other delivery path.
A transient disconnection is treated as a repair trigger and starts a full reconstruction.
A partially initialised copy (metadata cleared, cursor or generation not yet written) accepts deliveries or is presented as a copy.

constraint.text: Only the current leader may issue topology changes; recipients must reject obsolete authority.

controls.title: Authorize topology application
scenarios: An old reconcile resumes after lease takeover; a node has not yet heard the new generation.
assumptions: Lease availability and generation identity must be established; a newer generation fences only recipients that have observed it.
residual_risks: A check before sending cannot close the check/send race: the lease can be lost between the read and the first packet, or while the broadcast is in flight.

Recipient-side version fencing only protects a node that has ALREADY observed the newer generation; a node that missed the new leader's broadcast will accept an older leader's map. Per-node applied-generation tracking is SAF-09.
The post-send lease re-read records that the race occurred; it cannot retract what was sent.

Observed while building CHECK-01, not asserted on: after the lease is deleted and the SAME process re-acquires it, the operator was seen broadcasting a LOWER version than nodes already held, which their fencing rejects. The manipulation is cruder than a real takeover; treat as a lead for SAF-09.
The stop position is a test seam. It is inert without the environment variable and bounded at 120s, but it is production code that a misconfiguration could delay one broadcast with.

A suppressed send is retried only by a process that survives the suppression (lease read failure, momentarily foreign holder): the pending flag is in memory, and a confirmed lease loss ends the process, after which the next leader republishes from its own committed state. The retry test proves the flag was set by the withheld pass and consumed by the pass that published (that pass names the suppressed version); it does not prove the flag was NECESSARY for that send, because the committed version usually moves by itself within a pass.

Liveness (/healthz) is process-alive only and readiness treats a non-leader as ready. The operator that logged 'LOST LEASE -- exiting' and then hung — the Lean runtime waits for the never-ending server tasks before reporting the uncaught error — was therefore never restarted; that defect is fixed (IO.Process.exit) and CHECK-01 asserts the restart count moves, but a different stall of the main loop would still pass both probes.

The suite's evidence for 'the held pass did not send' is operator log lines read from the pod (across the designed restart); the checks are shape-based (fence for vHELD; a send line with old < new would be the held pass) rather than a wire-level capture. Two harness races (container replaced by the designed exit; retry line matching the negative check) were found by the CI runner's timing and fixed the same day; a third of the same family is plausible.

2026-10-01 (CI 36731888436): after the lease fence suppressed a broadcast, a newer commit superseded it before the retry, and the retry published the successor version instead of the withheld one; the test that names the suppressed version failed. Not data loss (survivors got the superseding map); the semantics of 'retry the withheld map' vs 'retry the current desired map' need the SAF-09 decision. RECLASSIFIED (2026-10-01): test premise, not a semantics gap. That pass was the restarted process's first, so its startup seed (v…306) was still pending when the fence withheld v…307; the flag keeps the earliest outstanding version and the retry publishes the latest committed map (documented design), so the line read pending v…306; publishing v…308. Test 4 now requires a retry line with pending ≤ held ≤ publishing. The FAIL record stays.

2026-10-01: the takeover test (b) ends on a check that every pod names the same master. Its held change is a read-balance weight, so the pre-takeover map already satisfies that check: it proves the exit and re-acquisition, not that the withheld map reached any pod or which path sent it. CHECK-01-startup adds the content and attribution check; the takeover test itself is unchanged.

Startup republish is tested only with the topology audit OFF (test seam FLARE_TEST_TOPOLOGY_AUDIT_OFF, inert when unset). With the audit on, a fresh process has two independent reasons to republish to a behind pod (startup seed, audit verdict=behind); the test shows the seed suffices, not how the two interact.

The send-reason record (broadcast trigger: ...) is logged with every send and is the attribution evidence; it is derived from the same four values the send condition uses (BroadcastTriggers.any), so it cannot disagree with the branch taken, but it is still a log line rather than a wire capture.

FINDING 2026-10-01 (CI 36831110279, not changed here): the persisted node map (serializeNodeMap) carries no read balance, so a reloaded map has every node at balance 100 until the first reconcile pass re-applies spec.readBalance and the SAF-10c read withholding. The operator answers node add from that in-memory map, and after a takeover the reloaded version is raised to the new generation base, newer than any pod holds. A flared pod that boots in that window adopts a map in which slaves, including WAL followers withheld from reads, carry balance 100, until the first pass pushes the corrected map seconds later. Running pods are not affected: flared requests the map only at boot. Side effect: with any slave weight other than 100, the first pass after a restart always advances the version, so the startup seed is rarely the only republish reason in practice. FIX (2026-10-01, CI pending): serializeNodeMap now persists each node's committed balance (balance=, including the SAF-10c withholding) and parseNodeMapLine restores it; a legacy line without the token loads as master 100 / others 0. Proved by nodeMapVersion_roundtrip (balances 100/0/25) and legacy_line_balance_fallback. The startup-republish E2E uses slave weight 25 again, so it fails if the reload changes the map.
controls.call_path: runReconcileFSMLoop -> commitClusterState -> (post-commit) lease check -> broadcastTopologyToAllPods. The FSM BroadcastTopology effect, which sent the unmerged map without a leadership check, has been removed; the effect constructor no longer exists.

checks.procedure: Run flare_unit observation cases: complete/truncated/duplicate stats; older/equal/newer version; missing/changing UID; new Unknown replaces old confirmation. Continuous-replication requires a UID-bound current observation from the production audit. Replacement during probe and startup republish as sole recovery remain unstaged.

Drive the production reconcile to a named stop position (committed, version advanced, pre-send lease check not yet made) using the FLARE_TEST_PRESEND_BARRIER seam, and confirm the position was reached by reading the held version the operator writes there. Topology changes are triggered by patching the FlareCluster readBalance spec (non-destructive). Then, for the same held pass: (a) retain the lease and require the release to broadcast that version - the control that proves the pass reaches the send at all; (b) hand the lease to another identity and require a fence log naming that version with no broadcast, then require the container restart count to move (losing the lease is designed to end the process), the restarted process to log lease acquisition, and the topology to be applied - exactly one Active master, every node Active, each flared's own `stats nodes` naming that master; (c) delete the lease and require the read-failure branch with no broadcast, then a later pass of the SAME process that publishes and names the suppressed version, and the applied topology. A receiver whose version does not move is not accepted as evidence on its own: a crash, a timeout or an exit before the branch look the same. Separately, push a mutated map at a stale version from inside the cluster and require flared both to keep its map and to log the rejection. Every test releases the barrier and restores authority before judging.

E2E topology-authority, test 'startup republish alone': hold one committed pass at the pre-send barrier (version H, a read-balance weight change), then replace the operator with a Deployment rollout that sets FLARE_TEST_TOPOLOGY_AUDIT_OFF=1 while the pass is held, so the map is persisted and never sent. Require: the operator pod was replaced; the fresh process logs the audit seam and no [TopologyAudit] probe; it resumed from the persisted map at a version >= H; its FIRST send's logged trigger record is pending-only (versionMoved=false, repairHeld=0, activeNotReady=0, pending=vX) and the matching broadcast line is (vX -> vX); every flared pod then reports node_map_version X AND the operator's committed slave balance in its own `stats nodes`, which must differ from what the pods showed before. Unit: BroadcastTriggers.any / pendingOnly / label cases in flare_unit.

constraint.text: A replica with missed writes remains repair-pending until reconstruction completes and missing data is recovered.

controls.title: Repair dropped replica writes
scenarios: Drops during normal service, a drop while the gate is held, an unresolved destination, operator restart with the ledger persisted, a master counter reset, drops arriving after a repair's reconstruction began, a failed ledger save, and a corrupt/unreadable ledger at start.

A drop whose destination is a WAL-mode follower (SAF-10): the ledger entry is HELD under the follower's ownership (no demotion, no rebuild), CLOSED when the follower's contiguous applied position reaches the master's position at request time in the SAME source epoch, HANDED OVER to the rebuild path only if the follower explicitly stops owning; an unreadable follower state (stats fetch failure) keeps the hold.
assumptions: Drop counters describe a source/destination incarnation (a counter that went down is a restart whose count is entirely new drops). flared keeps one completion RECORD per process — a random boot id, the latest reconstruction's id and state, and the id and source of the last success — so a completion can be tied to a process and a source; cumulative started/completed counters cannot (a failed handler leaves them unequal forever, a restart may reproduce their values).
residual_risks: A repair rebuilds the whole partition; there is no per-key repair.

Drops attributed after the reseat are requeued on completion; a drop in the LAST stretch of a live reconstruction is pinned by flare_unit, not staged end to end (a tiny dataset reconstructs within one pass).
The completion record is read over the stats channel; an unreadable record holds the entry (fail closed) rather than completing it.
A destination that became a MASTER while under repair is VOIDED, not repaired.
A write that keeps failing until a restart loses the unsaved delta; the window is one pass of retries, extended by however long the cause (e.g. a revoked RBAC grant) persists.

The operator announces an unsaved ledger ('marked unsaved and will retry every pass — an operator restart before that lands would lose ...') but a landing through the normal per-pass persist is silent, so the log does not show when that exposure ended (only the retry path logs 'persisted on retry'). Observability gap; follow-up proposed.

RBAC grant propagation: one local observation (2026-09-13) of ~131s before an impersonated `can-i` flipped after a restore; CI runs 6 and 8 saw the grant effective for the operator's own SA within seconds (in-pod probe). Earlier attributions of >2 minutes to the operator's path were harness artefacts (see the round-8 review note).

Until eb2ba17 the drop observation required the REPLICA's stats read to succeed as well as the master's, so an unreadable replica hid the master's drop counter for its partition (found by the SAF-10d stats-fetch-failure scenario, run 4). Fixed: the observation needs the master's reply only. E2E confirmation pending (run 5).

REGRESSION (found by rerunning replica-repair on tch after SAF-10c, fixed 2379cff): FollowReading treated a complete stats reply WITHOUT follower keys as unreadable, so every drop on a non-RocksDB replica was held as 'follower state unknown' and never repaired. Unknown now means a failed or truncated read only. The rerun of the non-WAL suites on the fix is pending.
controls.call_path: queue_proxy_write records destination drops -> stats proxy_write_dropped[dest] -> Main observe (only while the ledger is AVAILABLE; a partially corrupt ledger is unavailable, not smaller) -> ReplicaRepair ledger (persisted; dirty writes retried) -> demote to Proxy held out of assignment -> node confirms (boot id, current id, drops at reseat recorded) -> FSM re-seats Slave/Prepare -> flared reconstructs -> complete when the LATEST reconstruction SUCCEEDED from the current master and is newer than the reseat one in the same process, or in a new process (boot id changed); late drops requeued.

checks.procedure: Against real flared: cut master->slave traffic on the node (iptables REJECT), write keys, confirm the master counts proxy_write_dropped and the slave's LOCAL curr_items falls behind. Heal, then require REQUEST (log, status entry, metric), DEMOTE and HOLD, the node's CONFIRMATION, RE-SEAT and a reconstruction that began after it and finished (flared started/completed), COMPLETE, empty ledger, slave curr_items reaching the master's, no further drop. SAF-05: with FLARE_RESYNC_ON_DROP=0 the drop is HELD, survives an operator restart, and is repaired once the gate opens. Ledger faults: with the operator's write to flareclusters/status revoked, a new request is marked UNSAVED, retried each pass, absent from status, lands when the permission returns, and survives a restart; with status.replicaRepairs corrupted, the restarted operator reports the ledger UNAVAILABLE (never starts fresh), accounts no drop meanwhile, and once the ledger is repaired requests and recovers the drop seen during the outage.

flare_unit pins the ledger decisions on flared's completion record: release records boot id/current id/drops; a re-announced Active, a newer reconstruction still running, a newer one that FAILED, or a success from another source is NOT completion; a success newer than the reseat one completes; failure-then-success completes; a RESTART with identical counters completes because the boot id differs; a restart still running does not; late drops requeue exactly the increment; a partially corrupt ledger (missing masterKey, malformed counter, unknown phase, one bad among good) fails as a whole.

RocksDB, repl-identity-forward and repl-follow-enabled on for every node, replica read balance 0: verify both flags on all pods; write and see the replica apply forwarded changes through the common rule while following; cut master<->replica (iptables REJECT both ways), create/update/delete on the master until proxy_write_dropped is counted and stops increasing, STOP writing; heal and require the replica to resume from its applied_lsn to the master's position at the cut while following, item counts equal and the updated/created keys read correctly by DIRECT replica reads, reconstruction_started unchanged and the pod uid unchanged; require the ledger entry to be logged HELD as owned by the follower and then CLOSED by continuous replication with no demotion and no hand-over, status.replicaRepairs empty. Separately, with the operator's pods/exec revoked (inert resource name, original list restored after), a new drop is HELD as 'follower state unknown (stats unreadable)', never demoted while blind, and CLOSED once the probe returns.

constraint.text: Normal promotion and Prepare activation require a completed usable copy associated with the current source.

controls.title: Require valid synchronization evidence
scenarios: A Prepare slave whose activation was lost to an index-leader handover (reconstruction finished, operator still sees Prepare); a node with a PAST success that is now re-reconstructing (in flight); a RocksDB reply missing lineage or cursor (truncated); a zero cursor; a mismatched lineage; a cursor ahead of the head; a master or lineage change mid-observation; a fresh process.

SAF-10c: a WAL-mode follower as promotion candidate — proven current (following the master's current epoch, fresh by the node's own clock, lag within the promotion bound) is preferred; disconnected/stale/lagging/unreadable is unproven (no planned promotion, last resort for failover, logged NOT LOSS-FREE); needs_rebuild/initial_sync/idle/another epoch is unfit (never promoted by the FSM paths).
assumptions: flared exposes a per-process completion record in stats, read as ONE locked snapshot: reconstruction_boot_id (random per process), reconstruction_current_id/_state (latest handler), reconstruction_last_success_id/_source. Every notification carries the id the handler was given at begin(), so an older handler finishing after a newer one started cannot record the newer id as succeeded; last_success only advances and only the current handler's notification changes current_state. Activation requires the LATEST reconstruction to have succeeded from the current master. On RocksDB a completed reconstruction seeds a nonzero cursor and rocksdb_master_id identifies the source; the backend is told from a COMPLETE master reply.
residual_risks: Covers Prepare ACTIVATION by the repair path only; promotion still trusts the Active designation (SAF-08).

On a backend that reports no lineage/cursor (complete reply, no rocksdb_ keys) a completion with none in flight is accepted; the vacuous-activation guard in reconcileStep still requires an Active master to have synced from.
The prepare-evidence E2E runs on the tch backend, so the RocksDB lineage/cursor requirement is pinned by flare_unit, not staged end to end.

SAF-10c: failover with the master gone cannot prove currency (asynchronous replication); the FSM still promotes for availability and only logs that it is not loss-free. The TCP-side zombie-master guard (Reconciler.findActiveSlaveForPartition) does not consult follower evidence. Audit follow-up withholds never-read replicas until their mode is established (unit tested); independent stale-map routing and the amended read-value E2E are not yet executed. Prior E2E evidence does not validate this new local read guard.

The planned-promotion E2E (CHECK-04-follow) failed once on CI (run 36748059941) because the master was deleted inside a freshly restarted operator's 120 s startup grace period, during which drain and dead detection are skipped; no promotion of any kind happened and the recreated master re-registered. Harness precondition (fixed: the test waits for the operator to be older than 150 s); the operational consequence stands — a planned master removal within two minutes of an operator (re)start is not drained.

The planned-promotion E2E has never found the operator's 'graceful drain' line on CI even when it passes; it establishes that the proven follower is promoted and the epoch advances, not that the drain path (rather than failover after the preStop window) carried it. The drain-path exclusion of unproven followers therefore remains unit-pinned only.

2026-10-01 diagnosis of the drain caveat (CI pending): the startup grace is 24 reconcile CYCLES, not 120 s; with 2-3 s passes in the continuous-replication suite they last ~190 s, so the test's wait for a 150 s-old operator still deleted the master inside the grace, where the operator skips drain and dead detection. The follower was then promoted ~35 s later by dead-node failover once grace ended, which is why no drain line ever appeared (the terminating-pod suite, with fewer probes, does observe the drain). The test now waits for the operator's own 'grace period: 0 cycles remaining' line and REQUIRES the drain line; earlier PASS records on CHECK-04-follow proved promotion of the proven follower and the epoch advance, not the drain path. Separately: a grace measured in cycles stretches with slow passes; whether it should be wall-clock is a design question.

FINDING 2026-10-01 (CI 36841064685, functional): with the grace wait fixed, the drain ran but its guard REFUSED the proven follower ('NO promotable successor'); the follower was promoted ~35 s later by dead-node failover. Cause: the follow-evidence probe read the master's head only from pods that were Ready AND not Terminating, and during a drain the master is Terminating by definition, so no follower could be proven current and every planned promotion in follow mode was refused. Production impact: a planned master restart in follow mode did not hand off during preStop; writes in the preStop window and the gap until failover were served by a master about to exit. FIX (CI pending): the master's head is read from any Ready pod, Terminating included; the planned-promotion E2E now fails when the guard refuses.
controls.call_path: flared finishes reconstruction and calls activate_node; if the operator returned OK but did not persist it (leader handover) the node stays Prepare in the operator map. Main 4c builds a per-node episode, reads flared stats (reconstruction_completed, rocksdb_master_id, cursor + master head), SyncEvidence.judge requires a completed reconstruction bound to the current master's lineage with a sane cursor and unchanged source, and a positive verdict re-derives Prepare->Active through Reconciler.reconcileStep.

checks.procedure: Stage the lost activation with the TCP-server seam (FLARE_TEST_DROP_NODE_STATE) so the slave's reconstruction completes while the operator keeps it Prepare; assert the seam dropped an event and reconstruction_completed >= 1 (persistent signals), then that the repair activates on the NAMED evidence (N reconstruction(s) completed, none in flight; backend classification) and not on a cursor distance, applied through reconcileStep.

flare_unit pins SyncEvidence.judge on the completion record: latest running / failed / aborted refused; success from another source refused; #0 refused; the first review's LSN-0 input refused (cursor not seeded); lineage mismatch, cursor ahead, missing RocksDB lineage/cursor, and an incomplete master reply refused; failure-then-success (#2 succeeded after #1 failed) and abort-then-success ACCEPTED; a new process's own success accepted; a far-behind seeded cursor accepted; non-RocksDB accepted on the record; a source change refused until a success from the new master with matching lineage.

cutter test_stats_reconstruction pins the record's id binding: A begins #1, B begins #2, A succeeds -> current #2 still running, last_success #1 (not #2); a late success of an older handler does not regress a newer one; an older handler's failure or abort does not change the current state; a current failure after an earlier success leaves last_success != current so a controller must not activate.

flare_unit pins FollowEvidence.judge (unreadable → unknown; mode off → notInMode; not following, another epoch, stale observation, lag over the bound, applied ahead of the head → ineligible; unreadable master → unknown; lag at the bound eligible; read vs promotion bounds), unfitReason, classify (ranked highest-applied first; unproven vs unfit; withheld reads; mode memory; remembered-in-mode unreadable/not-probed → unproven and withheld, never unfit; no master reading → nothing proven), the probe policy, shapePromotionCandidates (unfit removed, ranked first, unproven last, nodeMap untouched, findActiveSuccessor sees the order, all-excluded leaves no successor), withholdReads (slave 0, master/Down/unlisted untouched, keys preserved) and the masterless refill's exclusion.

Invoke production pre_proxy_read with a stale positive slave balance: caught-up permits local read, disconnected and lagging attempt master enqueue rather than local read, recovery permits local read again, wrong source refuses local read. A deliberately unavailable transport proves fail-closed branch selection, not successful network delivery; real socket E2E remains required.

constraint.text: Delete only a revalidated target when independent current evidence supports the surviving copy.

controls.title: Protect copies before deleting Pods
scenarios: An empty-master candidate whose stats are missing/truncated (must not read as empty); a successor demoted by a resync between observation and delete; the target pod replaced under the same name; the operator losing its lease before the delete.

SAF-10c: the surviving copy is a WAL-mode follower — the delete proceeds only if, from the same fresh stats read at revalidation, it is following the master's current epoch, fresh, and within the promotion lag bound; unknown or ineligible refuses.
assumptions: curr_items is local storage; a stats reply with no well-formed curr_items line carries no information. A StatefulSet reuses a pod NAME for a replacement, so identity is the pod UID. The leader lease is the operator's authority to act.
residual_risks: Graceful deletion still does not guarantee a successful handoff; the drain guard protects a master with no promotable successor.
The successor/lease revalidation and the delete are not one atomic step; the pod-identity hole is closed by the API precondition, a successor demoted in the instant after the gate remains a window.

The direct-API delete is bounded (connect 3s, total 10s, outer wall 20s + 5s kill grace, ~25s worst case). A timeout or transport failure is an UNKNOWN deletion outcome — the API may have accepted the delete and only the reply was lost — and is reported as such; the caller keeps the streak and re-observes the pod on the next probe rather than assuming 'not deleted' or retrying blindly.

A live empty master with a data-bearing successor and an interposed change is not staged end to end; the gate is unit-pinned, the precondition and the deadline are staged by E2E against a replaced pod and a black-hole server.

SAF-10c: the survivor's currency is judged from one fresh reading at revalidation; a follower that disconnects in the instant after the gate remains a window (same shape as the successor-demotion window). Unit-pinned only.

Until d9d1285 storage_rocksdb::open seeded curr_items from rocksdb.estimate-num-keys, which does not count keys recovered from the WAL: after a crash the count under-reported by the unflushed tail (SAF-10d run 9: 52 keys present, not counted), so a count-based comparison could read intact data as loss — or, on a small DB, an intact master as empty. Fixed by an exact scan at open; unit-pinned (test_reopen_counts_wal_only_keys_exactly) and observed in E2E run 10.
controls.call_path: Main 4d probes master/slave curr_items -> parseCurrItems -> emptyMasterVerdict -> streak >= 3 -> REVALIDATE: pod UID, fresh stats, UID again, live map AFTER the stats, leader lease -> deleteGate -> Bridge.deletePodWithUidPrecondition: DELETE with DeleteOptions.preconditions.uid = the observed UID, refused by the apiserver (409) if another pod holds the name -> drain path.

checks.procedure: Malformed/empty/truncated stats must not delete a master; act only on a confirmed empty master with a confirmed data-bearing successor; revalidate stats, then the live map, then the lease, with the target UID stable across the observation; the delete carries the observed UID as an API-side precondition. E2E (replica-repair test 7) runs the operator's exact delete command inside the operator pod: accepted (200/202) for the matching UID, and refused (409) for a same-name replacement with another UID, which survives. Deadline (test 12): the same command aimed at a server that ACCEPTS the connection — proved server-side by the bytes the black hole received — and never answers ends by curl's TIMEOUT (exit 28) within the deadline; a refused connection (exit 7) does not pass this test, and the caller is told the outcome is unknown, not 'not deleted'.

flare_unit pins parseCurrItems (blank/missing/non-numeric are unknown, genuine 0 is known 0), emptyMasterVerdict (act only on known-0 + known data-bearing), successorStillValid (invalid when not data-bearing, demoted to Proxy, or the target is no longer an Active master), and deleteGate (refuses when the OPERATOR lost its lease, the pod UID changed, the successor is invalid on the post-read map, or the fresh verdict is skip).
flare_unit pins deleteGate's survivorFollowOk: an unproven surviving follower refuses the delete with a reason naming continuous replication; the survive purpose uses the promotion bound.

constraint.text: A future replication design must specify what acknowledged writes survive and how replicas catch up after interruption.

controls.title: Bound replication durability guarantees
scenarios: Replica unavailable through WAL retention; asynchronous drop after client success; master failover.

SAF-10 answers this control's subject on the RocksDB backend: the design states what a replica may claim (a contiguous applied position, never a connection or a past reconstruction) and how it catches up after an interruption (resume from the cursor; explicit needs_rebuild when the history is gone). Implementation and evidence live under EV-16..EV-20; acknowledged-write semantics are UNCHANGED — forwarding is still asynchronous and a write acknowledged to the client can still be lost if the master dies before the follower applies it.
assumptions: Current live replication is op-level forwarding; WAL is used for reconstruction/bootstrap only.
residual_risks: No continuous WAL replication; adding master LSNs alone does not establish durable acknowledgement semantics.

Replication is still asynchronous end to end: the master answers the client before the follower has applied, so continuous WAL replication removes the SILENT-gap failure, not the loss window on master death (design §5.3; the FSM logs an unproven promotion as NOT LOSS-FREE).

RESOURCE FLOOR, found by the scale evaluation (report 2026-09-21-saf10d-t6-t9-scale.txt): flared's RocksDB defaults budget ≈704 MB (512 MB block cache + 3 × 64 MB write buffers) before flared's own memory, so a 512Mi container is OOMKilled under write load (observed, exit 137 at 2m42s of a 2M-key load). The shipped chart's node default is limits.memory 1Gi and the FlareCluster CRD exposes no blockCacheSizeMb / writeBufferSizeMb / maxWriteBufferNumber, so the floor cannot be lowered through the chart. Not fixed in this PR.

WAL retention cap overshoot (from the SAF-10 long-outage evaluation, report 2026-09-30-sustained-after-more-fix.md): with a trailing follower the archive grew to 499 MB past a 256 MB cap before any purge; on tmpfs this is RAM. The chart's tmpfs guidance ('cap it well under tmpfs.sizeLimit') must account for the overshoot, not just the cap.

constraint.text: History loss is an explicit rebuild state.

controls.title: History loss is an explicit rebuild state
scenarios: The source answers lsn_purged, epoch_mismatch, master_id_mismatch or the cursor is ahead of the source: the follower declares needs_rebuild with the reason and stops; the operator turns the declaration into a repair-ledger request (no drop counter needed) and runs demote -> hold -> reseat -> reconstruction; an incomplete snapshot restore (sentinel present) refuses to open; a copy in needs_rebuild/initial_sync is unfit for promotion.
assumptions: flared reports the follower state truthfully in stats; the operator can read it (an unreadable state is Unknown, not synchronised).
residual_risks: A follower that declares needs_rebuild in the window between a completed reconstruction and its follower restart could be requested twice (bounded churn, not loss).

Until 325a2f8 the follower handler RETURNED on needs_rebuild, giving its thread back to the pool while cluster still referenced it; the later stop_wal_follower shut down a pooled thread, which exited without leaving the pool, and the reconstruction handler that was to rebuild the node was triggered on that dead thread and never ran (found by the SAF-10d bulk-operation scenario, runs 3-4). Fixed: terminal outcomes park the thread until the controller's shutdown. E2E confirmation pending (run 5).

After a source-epoch change the master's forwarded ops are refused by the stale-session replica, retried and counted as drops, so in the E2E the DROP path requested the rebuild before the follower-declared request could (runs 5-6: entry with drops=2). The two paths race and converge on the same rebuild; the follower-declared path alone (no drop counted, e.g. a purge with no write traffic) is unit-pinned, not staged end to end.

RocksDB does not always report a purged position as NotFound: with the requested WAL file gone, GetUpdatesSince serves from the oldest surviving file. Before 3b7f38c the follower refused that first batch as a contiguity violation mapped to a TRANSIENT apply error and retried it forever (T6 E2E: state=error/apply_error, applied position frozen while forwarding delivered). Fixed: the server answers lsn_purged when the first served batch is beyond lsn+1, and the client maps a gap refusal to lsn_purged → needs_rebuild. E2E confirmation (T6 purge suite) pending.

The two routes to a rebuild request (a counted drop and the follower's own needs_rebuild declaration) have each been OBSERVED to win in E2E and both orders are pinned sequentially by flare_unit, but true concurrency is NOT verified: nothing exercises them racing within one reconcile pass against the real persist path.
lsn_purged after an actual size-cap purge (not the 1 MB/1 s harness knobs) is now staged once: outage run 3 (6e757cb) — declared and rebuilt in 59 s. Single execution.

constraint.text: Both delivery paths apply through one comparison rule; no path may reorder, duplicate or resurrect, and every path that can change a key participates in the label capture.

controls.title: One comparison rule for both delivery paths
scenarios: Forwarded newer value then older WAL delivery leaves the newer value; the same change by both paths is applied once; a foreign session or stale incarnation is refused; a snapshot restore clears inherited metadata; the order label is captured under the slot lock for set/remove/incr; truncate/flush_all advance the source epoch instead of labelling; concurrent forwarded and WAL delivery decide under one lock; intra-batch repetition decides against the in-batch overlay; a batch with an unsupported operation or a count mismatch is refused.
assumptions: Every per-key write path in flared goes through set/remove (incr via set) so the label capture is complete; any new path must be added to the capture or switch the epoch.
residual_risks: Lock-hold time, forwarded-write wait and writer starvation under a far-behind replica are NOT measured (T17 deferred by agreement).
E2E coexistence scenarios T10-T13 are pinned by unit tests only; the minimal E2E shows forwarding-first then WAL re-delivery skipped.
controls.call_path: Master: set/remove capture entry.seq_label inside the slot lock -> queue_proxy_write stamps rl=<epoch>/<label> when repl-identity-forward is on -> op_set/op_delete send it. Replica: entry::parse reads rl= -> storage::apply_identified_change -> storage_rocksdb::apply_forwarded_change (shared apply lock + slot lock) -> _decide_change (session, cursor, per-key label) -> WriteBatch. WAL path: apply_wal_batch (exclusive) -> same _decide_change with in-batch overlays.

constraint.text: Delete history is discarded only when the applied position makes an older delivery impossible, and the decision is serialized with the write.

controls.title: Delete history discarded only by applied position, decided under the write lock
scenarios: A tombstone is collected only once the applied cursor has passed the delete's label; an old put arriving afterwards is refused by the cursor test, not by the (now absent) tombstone; collection runs inside the applier's exclusive window, chunked; a forwarded change stalled across a collection is refused when released.
assumptions: No wall-clock bound is used anywhere (design §9 decision 2).
residual_risks: The tombstone-space bound and its rebuild policy (design §9 decision 3) are not staged (T9 pending).
controls.call_path: apply_wal_batch (exclusive section) -> after the batch is written, _collect_tombstones_locked drops metadata rows with deleted=1 and label <= applied cursor, in chunks -> later deliveries at or below the cursor are refused by _decide_change before any per-key lookup.
